results.title: PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk (GOTO) to Hold Extraordinary General Meeting on Oct 14 2026 to Approve Capital Reduction and Director Resignation
results.body: The technology issuer PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk (GOTO) announced that it will convene an Extraordinary General Meeting of Shareholders (RUPSLB) on 14 October 2026 from 10:00 to 11:30 WIB. The meeting will consider two agenda items: a capital reduction that will cancel 32,186,417,803 treasury shares of Series A bought back between 12 June 2024 and 11 June 2025, and the resignation of Vice President Director Catherine Hindra, received on 28 August 2026. The capital reduction will amend GOTO’s articles of association and cancels a previously approved employee stock ownership program that had intended to allocate the buyback shares. Shareholders recorded on the shareholder list as of 21 September 2026, or holding shares in accounts at PT Kustodian Sentral Efek Indonesia (KSEI) at the close of trading on that date, are eligible to attend.

results.title: PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk (GOTO) seeks shareholder approval to cancel 32.18 billion treasury shares, with buyback program continuing
results.body: PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk (GOTO) is requesting shareholder approval at an extraordinary general meeting on 14 October 2026 to cancel approximately 32.18 billion treasury shares, representing 80.89% of its total treasury holdings of 39.78 billion shares. The treasury shares were acquired through a buyback program from 12 June 2024 to 11 June 2025 that cost Rp2.09 trillion, and the company plans to eliminate them via a capital reduction rather than the previously intended ESOP/MSOP allocation. PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk (GOTO) also announced that a further buyback of up to Rp3.5 trillion will be carried out from 19 June 2026 to 18 June 2027, funded from internal resources and not from public offerings or debt. The cancellation is expected to increase earnings per share, and the meeting will also consider the resignation of Vice President Director Catherine Hindra Sutjahyo.

results.title: PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk (GOTO) to hold Oct 14 extraordinary shareholders meeting with 80‑person physical attendance limit
results.body: PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk (GOTO) announced that its extraordinary shareholders meeting (RUPSLB) will be held on 14 October 2026 with a hybrid format and a physical attendance cap of 80 participants on a first‑come‑first‑served basis. The meeting agenda includes approval to repurchase 32.18 billion Series A treasury shares bought back in 2024‑2025, thereby reducing the company's paid‑in capital, and the cancellation of a planned ESOP/MSOP share‑ownership transfer. Shareholders will also vote on the resignation of Catherine Hindra Sutjahyo from her position as Vice Director (Wakil Direktur Utama) of PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk (GOTO). At the close of trading on 22 September 2026, GOTO’s shares were unchanged at Rp50 per share, and the company recorded 464,713 single‑investor shareholders as of the end of August 2026.

results.title: Morgan Stanley And Co International Plc Sells Shares of GoTo Gojek Tokopedia
results.body: Morgan Stanley And Co International Plc sold 1,392,623,600 GoTo Gojek Tokopedia shares at IDR 29 per share, amounting to IDR 40,386,084,400, and lowered its holding from 81,695,133,384 shares (7.095%) to 80,302,509,784 shares (6.974%), a decline of 0.121 percentage points. The disposal, made for investment purposes, follows modest sell‑offs in other IDX stocks, including 11,400 CTRA shares on July 7 and 1,293,000 AMRT shares on June 3, indicating a broader portfolio repositioning.

results.title: Morgan Stanley And Co International Plc Buy Shares of GoTo Gojek Tokopedia
results.body: On Sep 11, Morgan Stanley And Co International Plc purchased 420,000,000 GoTo Gojek Tokopedia shares at IDR 28 per share, costing IDR 11,760,000,000 and raising its stake to 7.095% from 7.059%. The buy adds to a series of recent acquisitions, including 3,138,522,500 shares at IDR 23 on Aug 26 and 9,221,177,326 shares at IDR 25 on Sep 7, underscoring a continued accumulation strategy by the institution.

results.title: IDNFinancials weekly roundup highlights Djarum Group's planned control of Narasi media, the INRU export case, and Danantara's disputed Rp120 trillion state deposit
results.body: The weekly most-read articles on IDNFinancials.com for September 7-13, 2026 center on three major domestic stories: Djarum Group's move to control Narasi media founded by Najwa Shihab, the INRU export case implicating Djarum as a suspect, and controversy over Danantara's Rp120 trillion deposit to the state treasury ordered by President Prabowo Subianto. Other top corporate stories include Bank Mandiri (BMRI) issuing US$750 million dollar bonds at a 7.35% coupon, Bumi Resources (BUMI) acquiring 100% of Loyal Metals, and Morgan Stanley increasing its stake in GoTo Gojek Tokopedia (GOTO) while shares trade at Rp50. President Prabowo's mandate for universal bank account ownership assigns roles to Bank Rakyat Indonesia (BRI) and Bank Syariah Indonesia (BSI), while the Whoosh high-speed rail project undergoes an 80-year debt restructuring.

results.title: Morgan Stanley Executes Rp186.64 billion Repo and Sell‑Buy of PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Shares Ahead of BEI Floor‑Price Adjustment
results.body: Morgan Stanley carried out a large sell‑buy and repurchase agreement of PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia shares ahead of the Bursa Efek Indonesia's planned floor‑price change. On 4 September 2026, it transacted 7.4 billion shares via the Negotiated Market (NG), including a repo of 1.45 billion shares at Rp27 and 5.95 billion shares at Rp25, valued at roughly Rp186.64 billion. The transaction reduced Morgan Stanley’s ownership in PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia from 7,3801 % to 6,9897 %, though the exposure remains indirect and non‑controlling. PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia’s shares remain at the Rp50 floor price, which BEI intends to lower to Rp1 later in September, while the company posted Q2 2026 net profit of Rp252 billion, revenue of Rp5.7 trillion and Group Adjusted EBITDA of Rp1.01 trillion.

results.title: GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Insider Morgan Stanley And Co International Plc Reports Shareholding Change
results.body: On Sept 7, 2026 Morgan Stanley And Co International Plc acquired 1,829,494,000 GoTo Gojek Tokopedia shares at IDR 27 per share, costing IDR 49,396,338,000. The purchase raised its holding from 80,476,862,884 shares (6.990%) to 82,306,356,884 shares, increasing its ownership to 7.149% of the company. The transaction is recorded as an investment.

results.title: GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Insider Morgan Stanley And Co International Plc Reports Shareholding Change
results.body: Morgan Stanley And Co International Plc sold a total of 7,402,292,100 GoTo Gojek Tokopedia shares on September 4, 2026, comprising 1,453,847,400 shares at IDR 27 and 5,948,444,700 shares at IDR 25, for a total consideration of IDR 187,964,997,300. The disposal reduced its holding from 84,971,460,184 shares (7.380%) to 80,476,862,884 shares (6.990%). The transaction was executed as an investment‑related share sale.

results.title: Morgan Stanley And Co International Plc purchases 21.67 billion GOTO shares at 50% discount via negotiated market
results.body: Morgan Stanley And Co International Plc acquired 21.67 billion shares of PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk through three negotiated market transactions on September 2, 2026, at Rp25 per share, a 50% discount to the regular market price of Rp50. The total outlay reached Rp541.97 billion, raising Morgan Stanley's ownership in GOTO to 7.59% from 5.71% at the end of August 2026. Morgan Stanley stated the purchases were not intended to maintain control over GOTO. The accumulation occurred just before GOTO's removal from the Morgan Stanley Capital International (MSCI) global index on August 31, 2026, after MSCI determined the stock no longer met liquidity criteria and had stagnated at Rp50 for over three months.

results.title: Morgan Stanley & Co International Plc purchases additional PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk shares worth Rp541.9 billion, raising its stake to 7.59%
results.body: Morgan Stanley & Co International Plc bought more shares of PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk after the company was removed from the MSCI index. On 2 September 2026 the broker purchased about 21.67 billion GOTO shares at Rp25 per share, spending roughly Rp541.98 billion and increasing its total holding to 87.48 billion shares, or 7.59% of the float, following an earlier purchase of 3.8 billion shares at Rp23 per share for about Rp87.3 billion at the end of August 2026. PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk reported net profit of Rp607 billion and revenue of Rp10.99 trillion for the first half of 2026, with revenue contributions of Rp3.2 trillion (+16.5%) from delivery services, Rp3.15 trillion (+14.9%) from services compensation, Rp2.71 trillion (+65%) from loan services, Rp551 billion (+32.3%) from Tokopedia e‑commerce service fees, Rp254 billion (+8%) from advertising, and Rp1.13 trillion (+46.5%) from other sources. The company is also considering a reverse stock split and a share buyback of up to Rp3.5 trillion, while analysts note that the removal of the price‑floor rule could ease passive‑fund pressure on the stock.

results.title: GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Insider Morgan Stanley And Co International Plc Reports Shareholding Change
results.body: On September 2, 2026, Morgan Stanley And Co International Plc increased its stake in GoTo Gojek Tokopedia by purchasing 12,697,825,600 shares at IDR 25 per share, valued at approximately IDR 317,445,640,000. The acquisition raised the institution’s holding from 75,029,997,584 shares (6.517% of the company) to 87,487,916,784 shares, representing a 1.082 percentage‑point increase to 7.599% of outstanding shares. The transaction was made for investment purposes.

results.title: PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk records Rp322 billion unrealized loss as PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk stock stalls at Rp50
results.body: PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk’s investment in PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk has incurred a large unrealized loss after GoTo shares remained at the Gocap level of Rp50 per share. On Monday 7 September 2026 the shares traded at Rp50 with a volume of 25.20 million shares and a transaction value of Rp1.26 billion, and Telkomsel, as reported in Telkom’s consolidated financial statements as of 30 June 2026, valued the shares at Rp50 each, with the unrealized loss amounting to Rp322 billion. Telkomsel’s CFO Daru Mulyawan stressed that the stock price does not fully reflect the strategic partnership and that the company will continue to evaluate the investment and synergy realization before deciding on further actions.

results.title: List of LQ45 stocks with lowest and highest PER on 2 September 2026, highlighting DEWA and AADI
results.body: The article lists the LQ45 index stocks with the lowest and highest price‑earnings ratios (PER) on 2 September 2026, highlighting PT Darma Henwa and PT Adaro Andalan Indonesia. Trading volume fell as the total transaction value dropped to Rp16.8 trillion from Rp20.7 trillion, and foreign investors posted a net sell of 5.59 billion shares worth Rp326.6 billion. PT Adaro Andalan Indonesia declined 2.07% and PT Darma Henwa slipped 2.16%, while PT Amman Mineral Internasional fell 2.06%, PT United Tractors dropped 2.05%, PT Bukit Asam rose 1.87%, and PT Indah Kiat Pulp & Paper held the lowest price‑to‑book value at 0.38 times. PT Japfa Comfeed Indonesia, PT Petrindo Jaya Kreasi, PT Bumi Resources, and PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia were largely stagnant, and six other LQ45 constituents each weakened by less than 2%, all of which are members of the LQ45 index as noted in the article.

results.title: The Fate of Indonesian Stocks Amid MSCI's Whirlwind
results.body: MSCI Inc’s August 2026 index review, effective 1 September, removed GOTO and CPIN from the MSCI Global Standard, leaving nine Indonesian constituents: UNTR, BBCA, BMRI, BBNI, BRMS, BBRI, BRPT, ASII and TLKM. During 1-2 September, foreign investors net bought the five most sought-after stocks—BBRI (Rp 993.29 bn), BBCA (Rp 589.83 bn), BMRI (Rp 227.78 bn), BBNI (Rp 36.34 bn) and BRPT (Rp 43.86 bn)—while net selling UNTR (Rp 10.11 bn), BRMS (Rp 54.06 bn), TLKM (Rp 111.7 bn) and ASII (Rp 65.92 bn). On the latest trading day, BBRI rose 0.30% to Rp 3,390, BBCA jumped 1.14% to Rp 6,675, BMRI gained 0.93% to Rp 4,360, BBNI climbed 0.78% to Rp 3,900 and BRPT slipped 0.55% to Rp 1,820, while ASII fell 1.63% to Rp 4,840, TLKM dropped 0.77% to Rp 2,590, BRMS declined 1.37% to Rp 720 and UNTR slipped 2.05% to Rp 25,050. The divergent net foreign flows underscore varying investor sentiment among the remaining MSCI constituents after the index composition change.

results.title: Foreign Investors Net Sell TLKM and GOTO Shares
results.body: Foreign investors net sold shares of PT Telkom Indonesia (Persero) Tbk and PT Goto Gojek Tokopedia Tbk during the first session on September 2, 2026, on the Bursa Efek Indonesia. The net sell amounted to Rp 95.9 billion for 37.1 million shares of PT Telkom Indonesia (Persero) Tbk and Rp 92.5 billion for 1.85 billion shares of PT Goto Gojek Tokopedia Tbk. The sales coincided with a 1.92% decline in PT Telkom Indonesia (Persero) Tbk to Rp 2,560 and a stagnant price of Rp 50 for PT Goto Gojek Tokopedia Tbk, with year-to-date declines of 26.4% and 21.8% respectively. Overall, the activity reflects foreign investors’ continued pressure on these two Indonesian telecom and e-commerce conglomerates.

results.title: PT TBS Energi Utama Tbk’s EV Business Enters Monetisation Phase, Posting Positive Gross Profit and Adjusted EBITDA in H1 2026
results.body: PT TBS Energi Utama Tbk’s electric‑vehicle segment, operated through the Electrum joint venture with PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk, entered a monetisation phase in the first half of 2026. Revenue rose 184% year‑on‑year to US$9.06 million, gross profit turned positive at US$0.39 million (from a US$0.45 million loss) and adjusted EBITDA became positive at about US$0.5 million. The ecosystem now covers roughly 13,883 two‑wheel EVs (up 172%) and 550 battery‑swapping stations (up 72%), supporting over 1.7 million monthly swaps and more than 135 million km traveled, and Kiwoom Sekuritas analyst Abdul Azis said the profit shift signals healthier unit economics and a focus on utilisation to drive recurring revenue.

results.title: Commission cut and floor‑price removal raise new challenges for GoTo, says CEO and analysts
results.body: The article discusses how new ride‑hailing commission regulations and the planned removal of the Rp50 floor price create fresh challenges for PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk (GoTo). GoTo reported its first half‑year net profit of Rp608 billion for Jan‑Jun 2026, reversing a Rp580 billion loss a year earlier, and reaffirmed its 2026 adjusted EBITDA target of Rp3.2‑3.4 trillion. Effective 1 July 2026 the commission on two‑wheel transport apps is capped at 8 % down from 20 %, while the Indonesia Stock Exchange intends to drop the Rp50 minimum price, potentially allowing GoTo shares to trade as low as Rp1. Analysts from MNC Sekuritas and Kiwoom Sekuritas note that the floor‑price change could ease technical overhang and improve liquidity, while Morgan Stanley disclosed a purchase of GoTo shares at Rp23, giving it about 5.2 % of the outstanding stock. The company’s ecosystem, with Gojek and GoPay as subsidiaries, is expected to rely on continued regulatory flexibility to sustain its profitability.

results.title: CPIN drops after MSCI downgrade as foreign investors sell heavily on Aug 31
results.body: PT Charoen Pokphand Indonesia Tbk (CPIN) was the most heavily sold stock after MSCI moved it from the MSCI Main Index to the MSCI Global Small Cap on Monday, 31 August 2026. Foreign investors recorded a net sell of Rp710.56 billion in the regular market, with CPIN alone seeing a net sell of Rp681.76 billion covering 228.42 million shares. The Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) edged up 0.11% to 6,525 despite the selling pressure. Ten issuers were removed from MSCI, including PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia Tbk (GOTO) which was taken off the MSCI Main Index.

results.title: IHSG projected sideways‑bearish for September 2026 with key support at 6,400‑6,500 and stock picks from Phintraco and Sucor Sekuritas
results.body: The article projects Indonesia’s composite index (IHSG) to trade sideways‑bearish in September 2026, likely ranging between 6,400 and 6,700 points with support at 6,400‑6,500 and resistance near 6,700. Analysts cite a forward P/E of 9.8×, a stable BI‑Rate of 5.75%, and a 1.11% rupiah appreciation to Rp17,876/USD as factors supporting a modest outlook, while historical September performance shows an average gain of only 0.02% over 20 years and a 10‑year average loss of 0.94%. Phintraco Sekuritas analyst Alrich Paskalis Tambolang recommends BBCA, BMRI, TLKM, ASII and PGEO with target prices of Rp6,800, Rp4,500, Rp2,800, Rp5,300 and Rp1,150 respectively. Sucor Sekuritas manager Hendry Wijaya suggests BRMS, INET, VKTR, TAPG, TINS and PTRO with target‑price ranges and cut‑loss levels as listed. The MSCI rebalancing effective 1 September, which removed several small‑cap stocks and re‑classified GOTO and CPIN, is noted but not expected to drive a sharp index decline.
